Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

original adjective

new, not copied; of a person, inventive

also originality, inventive, creative, novel, an original idea

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.13: nova et ā nōbīs inventa ratiō
Cic. Rep. 1.21: nihil novī vōbīs adferam, neque quod ā mē sit cōgitātum aut inventum

novus, nova, novum

adjective, declension

new, novel, original

An original idea is new and one’s own: novum et ā mē inventum, new and found by me. See new.

Other words

  • inaudītus, inaudīta, inaudītum — unheard of, quite new

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 36: novum est, nōn dīcō inūsitātum, vērum omnīnō inaudītum

    A favourite word of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).

  • ingeniōsus, ingeniōsa, ingeniōsum — of a person: inventive, clever, gifted

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 32: talented, ingeniōsus

  • orīginālis, orīgināle — from the origin, first

    adjective, third declension · avoid · late Latin · Apul. M. 11.2: Cerēs … frūgum parēns orīginālis (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin, and only of what comes first or from the source (see original: first); it never meant new or inventive.

Examples

  • Nūllum est jam dictum quod nōn dictum sit prius.

    Nothing is said now that has not been said before.Ter. Eun. 41

  • Nihil novī vōbīs adferam, neque quod ā mē sit cōgitātum aut inventum

    I shall bring you nothing new, nothing thought out or discovered by meCic. Rep. 1.21

  • similem esse tē volō quōmodo fīlium, nōn quōmodo imāginem: imāgō rēs mortua est

    I want you to resemble your model as a son does, not as a portrait does: a portrait is a dead thingSen. Ep. 84.8

See also new, original, clever.
